reason: The talk states rainfall 'stayed right around the region's long-term average' and separately rules out a slow drying trend (A), wild wet-dry swings (C) and an unusual wet period (D).
Residue analysis is called 'unambiguous' for olive oil pressed on site, with barley, imported wine and fish each explicitly excluded.

The professor says he raises Kessara 'for one reason' — its newer methods, which he wants at Arvani — and explicitly disclaims simultaneous collapse (A), tablet references (C) and any settled view on later continuation (D).

'Shaking may explain some of the damage. It doesn't, by itself, explain why nobody came back' is stated verbatim; the damage is said to fit the date not centuries earlier (A), to be no slow decay (D), and 'half right' rules out calling it the best-supported account (B).

Uplift 'went on climbing... long after the earthquake swarms had stopped', while the talk denies a narrower area (A), any rise-and-fall cycle (C), and places the uplift squarely over the centre, not a western rim (D).
The talk names a mixed magmatic-plus-hydrothermal source explicitly, and denies magma alone (A, which also adds an unstated 'stalling'), an old cooling body (B) and groundwater alone (C).

'The resemblance was the whole alarm' answers the purpose question; observers are said to have read the signs correctly (A), the deposits are useless for mapping (B), and that episode ended in an eruption (D).
'The pressure was coming from the public, and the committee moved with it', against explicit denials of a forcing protocol (A), new instrumental support that week (B) and lateness (C).
Lapis is found everywhere including the border sprays, with no cheaper base layer (A), no azurite (B) and no indigo (C) anywhere in the book.
The professor flags the takeaway point as material governed by 'each patron's purse', and expressly denies a matching model book (A), stylistic conservatism (C) and confusion with Arden work (D).

Payments stopping in the third year is given as the reason the last two gatherings are unfinished; the accounts are said not to itemize pigments (B), not to date production closely (C) and never to name an assistant (D).

He affirms the attribution on the page architecture while calling the underdrawing too varied for one hand (B) and the faces assistants' work (C), and says every page falls within his working life (D).
'Nearly everything new is strung along the debris lines', with explicit denials of overall scarcity (A), recruitment under parent trees (B) and dry-season mortality (C).

The flocks are said to be too small to clear the crop before it drops and rots; rats were ruled out by exclosures (A), the vine never reached the feeding branches (B) and fruiting still matches the breeding season (D).

He states his question is whether mainland lessons transfer to an atoll, and explicitly disclaims a bird source (A), a claim that the problem stops at the shoreline (B) and a substitute-disperser argument (C).

A hand-carrying trial is 'already running on the island's two worst-hit stretches'; pigeon counts are still falling (A), the team is not opposed to intervening (B) and no translocation has been proposed (C).
'The shift comes after the borrowing' because Emel keeps the old vowels; the talk denies doubled forms (A), a completed shift at borrowing time (B) and the reverse direction (D).
'It follows the rivers' with 'no single center it radiates from'; households shifted together including parents (B), every word class moved at once (C) and no hint that careful speech led (D).
'The shift was done a century before the cylinders turned'; every recorded village shows shifted vowels (A), no speaker mixes systems (C) and the era's transcriptions are called rather good (D).

He says substrate loanwords carry precisely these vowels and that the idea 'stands'; the talk denies guessing without evidence (A), denies any revival since it has been argued continuously (B) and puts the substrate's range where the shift runs deepest (C).

'It was the pooling that did it' names the 1885 exchange with the Austrian network; barometers were the basis from day one (A), the fishing-crew scheme never left proposal stage (C) and the telegraph linked stations from the first season (D).

'I tell that story for one reason: it is the event that put the money on the table' — the stated single purpose forecloses the illustrative reading in C, and the talk denies both blame on the service (B) and any warning having been issued (D).

The recalibration team found readings consistently low by about two millibars; the ledgers survive nearly complete (A), are gathered in one Trieste archive (B) and climate researchers have shown no interest (C).

'A brilliant promoter... but his claims ran well ahead of what his barometers could show'; the public never lost faith (A), the organization was held together with string (B) and his statistics were ordinary (D).
The parts appear never to have been played from, 'a set made to be looked at'; rubbing is uniform across suites (A), which also blocks steady use (B), and nothing was added by later readers (C).

The Casperi letter is 'our only eyewitness account' of Fantin leading the suites; the band was about the same size as Welden's (A), the dedication names the Duke of Welden (B) and Casperi's payment books never mention the suites (D).

He answers yes on the repeat schemes matching the choreographies figure for figure; the court ledger tells us nothing either way (B), the match holds for every movement (C) and the tempo markings are called perfectly danceable (D).
